summary: PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19 is a careful extraction of Khayutin's 132-page Annals paper, and its review did substantial work. The published text was read and hashed, 59 statements were corrected, and 31 further source mistakes were found and checked. I re-read the whole published article against all 124 items, re-derived the key source issues and recounted the Appendix B densities by brute force. The main theorems are stated with exactly the paper's hypotheses: two fixed split primes, no Landau–Siegel zero, bounded conductor and the archimedean condition. The work breaks in eleven places. (1)–(4) Four items restate printed results that are false, and no source issue records them: Lemma A.6's dyadic unit norms (item 104, with μ_wild in item 119); Proposition 9.26's local factor and the hypothesis of Proposition 9.25 (item 87); Lemma 8.33 when a ∈ K_{p_1} (item 74); and the 'index-2' and 'compact' claims about the reduced-norm map (item 8). Each is checked by a counterexample, and none affects the main theorems (high). (5) Duke's theorem, in Linnik's adelic split-prime form, is used three times but has no item, and Linnik's book is not a prerequisite (medium). (6) The Huxley prerequisite is wrongly called unnecessary: without Huxley or a Ramanujan improvement the two ranges of §10.4 do not overlap. The Part II brief never plans the small-norm half of the proof, and the prerequisites the review flagged were never added (medium). (7) The genus-theory block routed to HE.0 extends the Tau Ceti Multiquadratic roadmap, whose maximal-order case is already built at f790474, and so belongs in MultiquadraticPartII (medium). (8) sourceVersions is missing, so the collation worklist wrongly treats the paper as read only in preprint (low). (9) Six more source slips, and incomplete corrections in E7, E12 and E13 (low). (10) Item-level slips, most introduced by the review (low). (11) Item 6 is only partly planned (low). 11 findings: 4 high, 3 medium, 4 low.
checked: Authorship. The extraction PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19 is by Claude Code cc-7b31c4 (issue #1131, commit fcbc7e3a, PR #1956, 22 September 2026). The review REV-PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19 is by Claude Code cc-39fac3 (issue #1132, commit 6542eb08, PR #2261, 23 September 2026). No errata record for this paper exists under research/blueprint/errata/, so there are no colliding ids; its source issues reach research/errata/REGISTER.md directly from the result file. The string cc-f805bf occurs in none of the target files, the .review.json or the review report. This session did none of that work. It red-teamed PAPER-NELSON-VENKATESH-21 (PR #4740) and wrote FIX-RT-AREA-automorphic-1; no finding here touches either.

Source (preprint). The paper is arXiv:1710.04557, not 1510.07627. The arXiv listing, read 30 September 2026, has v1 (12 Oct 2017), v2 (18 Oct 2017) and v3 (22 Oct 2018), the last, 'To appear in Annals of Math., updated following referee comments'. I fetched the v3 source archive (SHA-256 d76399f1…c110, matching the recorded hash) and the v3 PDF (118 pp., SHA-256 f740c420…3eb9).

Source (version of record). Ann. of Math. 189 (2019), 145–276, from https://annals.math.princeton.edu/wp-content/uploads/annals-v189-n1-p04-s.pdf, fetched 30 September 2026. Its SHA-256 f22691429c27058fabd47fe12c6a901e7feffffad7a0c52e1a936da645166d6f matches the review's. The Annals page gives Received 18 October 2017, Revised 15 October 2018, Accepted 22 October 2018, Published online 11 January 2019, and lists no erratum. Crossref for 10.4007/annals.2019.189.1.4 has no update-to, relation or updated-by. I read the published text through pdftotext in four section groups, each read in full against its items (§§1–3; §§4–7; §§8 and 10; §9 and Appendices A–B), with page images of pp. 162, 165–167, 170, 172, 177, 179, 183–190, 192, 194, 196, 198, 201 and of the pages quoted in the findings. Every finding here was checked by me at its locator.

All 124 items against the published statements and locators, with every hypothesis. The main theorems are faithful. Theorem 1.3: K_∞-invariant packets, fundamental D_i < 0, p_1 and p_2 split, no Landau–Siegel zero, 𝔑_i → ∞, conclusion a convex combination over the components of Y × Y. Theorem 1.4: G split over R, a common maximal order, two split primes, no exceptional zero, finite intersection with proper special subvarieties. Theorems 3.2 and 3.9: (1) g_∞^{−1}T(R)g_∞ = K_∞, (2) split p_1 and p_2, (3) no exceptional zero, (4) f_i ≪ 1, with |D_i| → ∞ and the genericity condition. Theorem 3.10 as printed. The review's restoration of f_i ≪ 1 and of the archimedean condition is correct. Items are faithful apart from findings 1–4, 9 and 10.

Coverage. Every numbered statement of §§1–10 and Appendices A–B has an item, except Remark 7.4 and the inessential Remarks 8.15, 8.22 and 8.31. External inputs were checked against the items and prerequisites: EL15a Th. 1.4, Cor. 1.5 and Lemma 7.4 (in the notes of items 23, 27 and 31 and in the prerequisites); Duke/Linnik (finding 5); Howe–Moore (item 29 note); strong approximation (AA.4 route); Hasse–Schilling–Maass (item 8); Siegel, Conrey–Iwaniec, Hecke–Landau, bounds towards Ramanujan and Huxley (finding 6); Shiu, Nair and Nair–Tenenbaum, Kowalski's large sieve, GKM15 and Schwartz–Zippel (in §9 items). Entropy enters only in Lemma 10.1 and §10.4 through [ELMV09, Prop. 3.2] and leafwise measures; §4 uses no entropy hypothesis. The paper does not use Heegner points, Eichler orders or Hecke operators beyond T_{p^m} in §10.4.

Source issues E1–E34, each at its locator in print. The quotations match. E5, E6, E9, E13, E25, E27 and E28 were re-derived. E30–E34 were confirmed by brute-force counts of solutions of binary quadratic forms modulo p^n (e.g. Lemma B.4 as corrected: 4,680 cases, no failure; Proposition B.8 with (−ω/p): 4,768/4,768). E20's gap stands; its estimate of the size of range R_2 is if anything too small. 'Same in arXiv v3' was checked for each sampled issue. Corrections needing change: E7, E12, E13 (finding 9).

Statuses and library. No item claims library status. In both pinned libraries (declarations index and source) I searched for joinings, equidistribution, measure rigidity, entropy, Heegner and CM points, quaternion orders, reduced norm, quadratic orders, orbital integrals, Bowen balls, Linnik, Duke, Siegel zeros, the large sieve, Huxley/van der Corput and strong approximation; none provides an item. Mathlib 082e2d3 has MvPolynomial.schwartz_zippel_totalDegree (Mathlib/Algebra/MvPolynomial/SchwartzZippel.lean:192), a near miss for item 76 that the item's note records correctly, and SelbergSieve (Mathlib/NumberTheory/SelbergSieve.lean:77), which no item needs. Tau Ceti f790474 has the Multiquadratic genus theory (finding 7). The planned statuses were checked: item 5 against AA.1 and AA.3 (correct); item 6 (finding 11).

Routes and owners. The five routes were checked against the stage texts in research/blueprint/atlas/roadmaps (GN.2, GN.4, SV.0–SV.2, HE.0, AA.1, AA.3, AA.4), the Tau Ceti READMEs GlobalNumberFields (layer 11), QuadraticFormInvariants (layers 2 and 7) and Multiquadratic (layers 1–3), and the packets: GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic and SieveMethodsAndPrimePatterns are partial, with GN.2, GN.4 and SV.0–SV.2 still partial; HeegnerPointEulerSystems in data/decompositions has HE.0 not_read; AdelicAlgebraicGroups has no packet. So no route goes into a finished blueprint. Route 1 merges into DESIGN-GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmeticPartII (pending), with no cycle. I compared other extractions: PAPER-DUKE-IMAMOGLU-TOTH-16 routes 1 and 10 (findings 5 and 7), PAPER-SHENDE-TSIMERMAN-17 route 4 (the function-field analogue in ArithmeticStatistics ST.5; different setting, no duplicate), PAPER-TSIMERMAN-18 route 9 and PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86 route 7 (CM heights, effective class numbers; no overlap with any item), and PAPER-NELSON-VENKATESH-21 (no overlap). No other extraction plans Einsiedler–Lindenstrauss joinings or measure rigidity.

Review changes. The 13 added items, 59 corrected statements, route 5 and the move of item 8 were checked. They are sound, except for the duplication of Lemma 5.10 between items 92 and 117 and the incomplete propagation of E25's repair (finding 10).

findings.where: PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19/104 (Lemma A.6); PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19/119 (Corollary A.7); sourceIssues (missing entry)
findings.claim: Item 104 states Lemma A.6 as printed, and its dyadic cases are false. For 2 ∥ 𝔣 the lemma gives Nr Λ_2^× = Nr O_{E_2}^×, which fails when 8 ∥ d_E. For 4 ∥ 𝔣 with Nr O_{E_2}^× = 1+4Z_2 it gives 1+4Z_2, which also fails: the true value is 1+8Z_2 in both cases. Item 119 inherits a false sentence from this: 'μ_wild depends only on 𝔣_2 and on the ramification of 2 in E'. The review corrected item 104 against print but kept this lemma, and no source issue records it.
findings.evidence: Published p. 259, Lemma A.6: 'If p = 2, then Nr Λ_v^× = Nr O_{E_v}^× if 2 ∥ f_v; = 1 + 4Z_2 if 4 ∥ f_v and E_v/Q_v is unramified or Nr O_{E_v}^× = 1 + 4Z_2; = 1 + 8Z_2 = Z_v^{×2} otherwise' (the same in arXiv v3). Check 1: E_2 = Q_2(√−2), 2 ∥ 𝔣. Then Λ_2 = Z_2 + 2O and its units are a + 2b√−2 with a odd. Their norms a² + 8b² are ≡ 1 mod 8, so Nr Λ_2^× = 1+8Z_2, while Nr O^× = {a² + 2b²} = {1,3}·Z_2^{×2}. Check 2: E_2 = Q_2(i), 4 ∥ 𝔣, so Nr O^× = 1+4Z_2. Then Λ_2 = Z_2 + 4Z_2[i], the norms are a² + 16b² ≡ 1 mod 8, and Nr Λ_2^× = 1+8Z_2, not 1+4Z_2. Check 3 (global): D = −32 = −8·2² has h(D) = 2, so #Pic(Λ)[2] = 2. The printed lemma gives μ_tame = 0 and μ_wild = 1, hence #Pic[2] = 2^{μ_tame+μ_wild−1} = 1, a contradiction; with the correct 1+8Z_2, μ_wild = 2 and the count is 2. A brute-force comparison of Nr Λ_2^× with #Pic(Λ)[2], counted from ambiguous reduced forms, agrees for every D ≥ −3000 once the lemma is corrected. The printed lemma fails for 59 of those D, exactly the two cases above. D = −16 and D = −32 have the same 𝔣_2 = 2, and 2 ramifies in both, yet μ_wild is 1 and 2, which contradicts the Corollary A.7 sentence.
findings.fix: Restate item 104's p = 2 clause: Nr Λ_2^× = Nr O_{E_2}^× if 2 ∥ 𝔣 and either E_2/Q_2 is unramified or Nr O_{E_2}^× = 1+4Z_2 (i.e. 4 ∥ d_E); = 1+4Z_2 if 4 ∥ 𝔣 and E_2/Q_2 is unramified; = 1+8Z_2 otherwise. In item 119 replace 'depends only on 𝔣_2 and on the ramification of 2 in E' by 'depends only on 𝔣_2 and on E_2 (equivalently ord_2 d_E)'. Add a source issue (kind error, affects 'a stated result', known new) at Appendix A.1, Lemma A.6 and its proof, p. 259 (arXiv v3: Lemma 159), with the checks above. Say that Corollary A.7's formula, Proposition A.10, Lemma A.14 and Definition 8.6 use the index only abstractly and so still hold.

findings.claim: Item 87 states both propositions as printed, and both are defective. (a) The bound in Proposition 9.26 is false as stated: it has ρ_Q(k_1l; k_1k_2) where the proof counts residue classes of Q ≡ k_0k_1l mod k_1k_2. (b) The curvature hypothesis added in Proposition 9.25, (R_max/k_0)^{θ_l} ≤ A(E)/k_0², does not give the hypothesis of Theorem 9.7 for the rescaled domain k_0^{−1}(E − r), which the proof ('A direct calculation shows …') needs. Neither mistake is recorded.
findings.evidence: Published p. 236, Proposition 9.26: the sum over '(x,y) ∈ E ∩ Z², Q(x,y) ≡ k_0k_1l mod k' is ≪ 'A(E) f(k_1)ρ_Q(k_1l; k_1k_2)/(k_1k_2)² ⋯'. The proof on p. 237 takes 'one of the ρ_Q(k_1l; k_1k_2) congruence classes modulo k_1k_2 solving … Q(x,y) ≡ k_1l mod k_1k_2'. By the Chinese remainder theorem the condition summed over is k_0 | Q together with Q ≡ k_0k_1l mod k_1k_2. Counterexample to the printed bound: Q = x² + 3y², f ≡ 1, k_0 = 2, k_1 = 1, k_2 = 3, l = 5 (a unit mod k = 6), E a large disc. The left side counts the points with Q ≡ 4 mod 6, e.g. (1,1), which are about a third of all points. The right side contains ρ_Q(5; 3) = #{x² ≡ 2 mod 3} = 0. Proposition 9.25, p. 235: 'Consider the setting of Theorem 9.7 but assume the stronger assumptions (R_max/k_0)^{θ_l} ≤ A(E)/k_0² and X ≤ A(E)^δ k_0^{1−2δ}.' Theorem 9.7 (p. 222) requires R_max^{θ_l} ≤ A(E)^{1−3η}. For k_0^{−1}(E − r) this reads (R_max/k_0)^{θ_l} ≤ (A(E)/k_0²)^{1−3η}. Counterexample: θ_l = 2/3, η = 0.1, A = 10^{12}, R_max = 10^7, k_0 = 10^{5.5}. Then R^{θ} = 10^{4.67} ≤ A^{0.7} and (R/k_0)^θ = 10 ≤ A/k_0² = 10, but (A/k_0²)^{0.7} = 10^{0.7} < 10. The same text is in arXiv v3.
findings.fix: In item 87 replace ρ_Q(k_1l; k_1k_2) by ρ_Q(k_0k_1l; k_1k_2), and replace Proposition 9.25's hypothesis by (R_max/k_0)^{θ_l} ≤ (A(E)/k_0²)^{1−3η}. Proposition 9.26's own hypotheses imply this: k² ≤ A^η gives (R/k)^θ ≤ A^{1−4η} ≤ (A/k²)^{1−3η}. Add two source issues (Proposition 9.26: kind error, affects a stated result; Proposition 9.25: kind gap, affects the proof). Note that Proposition 10.10 (p. 245) already applies the corrected form ρ_Q(m; (D_0D_1)²), so §10 is unaffected.

findings.claim: Item 74 states Lemma 8.33 as printed: for every n and every a ∈ A_{p_1}, the ratio m(K ∩ aKa^{−1}) / m(K^{(−n,n)} ∩ aK^{(−n,n)}a^{−1}) equals p_1^{2n}. This is false when a ∈ K_{p_1} (the case k = 0 of the proof, e.g. a = 1). There the ratio is (1 + 1/p_1)·p_1^{2n}. Nothing records the mistake.
findings.evidence: Published p. 218: 'For any n ∈ N and any a ∈ A_{p_1}, m(K_{p_1} ∩ aK_{p_1}a^{−1}) / m(K_{p_1}^{(−n,n)} ∩ aK_{p_1}^{(−n,n)}a^{−1}) = p_1^{2n}'. Proof, p. 218–219: 'a.x_0 = x_k for some k ≥ 0'. It counts vertices y_1 whose geodesic to x_0 'does not pass through x_1', and y_2 whose geodesic to x_k 'does not pass through x_{k−1}', giving p^n·p^n. For k = 0 the numerator subgroup is K = Stab(x_0), and the denominator subgroup is the stabiliser of the path x_{−n}…x_n. The ratio is the number of geodesic paths of length 2n with midpoint x_0, namely (p+1)p^{n−1}·p^n = (1 + 1/p)p^{2n}. The printed count excludes the p^{n−1} choices of y_1 that pass through x_1 and allows y_1, y_2 to leave x_0 along the same edge. For k ≥ 1 the lemma is right. In Theorem 8.7 (p. 219, 'For G^Δ, we use Lemma 8.33 …') the discrepancy is a factor at most 1 + 1/p_1 ≤ 3/2, which the implied constants absorb.
findings.fix: Restate item 74: the ratio is p_1^{2n} if a ∉ K_{p_1} and (1 + p_1^{−1})p_1^{2n} if a ∈ K_{p_1}; in every case it lies in [p_1^{2n}, 2p_1^{2n}]. Add a source issue at §8.8, Lemma 8.33, p. 218 (arXiv v3: Lemma 112), kind error, affects a stated result. Theorem 8.7 holds with a changed constant.

findings.claim: Item 8 says that the reduced-norm map on double cosets G(Q)\G(A)/G(A)^+ → Q^×\A^×/A^{×2} 'is onto in the split case and has index-2 image otherwise'. The index-2 claim is false: the map is onto whether or not B is split at ∞. The item also calls G(A)/G(A)^+ → A^×/A^{×2} a monomorphism 'of compact abelian groups', but neither group is compact. Both statements are copied from the paper (§2.3, repeated in the proof of Proposition 3.6), and neither is recorded as a source issue.
findings.evidence: Published p. 162: 'Nrd : B^× → G_m induces a monomorphism of compact abelian groups Nrd : G(A)/G(A)^+ → A^×/A^{×2}' and 'this morphism has full image if B is split at ∞ and the image is the index-2 subgroup Q_{>0}\R_{>0} × A_f^×/A^{×2} otherwise'. P. 172, proof of Proposition 3.6: 'This map is onto if B is split at ∞, and otherwise it is the index 2 subgroup …'. The same text is in arXiv v3. Argument: −1 ∈ Q^× has negative archimedean component, so Q^×·(R_{>0} × A_f^×) = A^×. The natural map Q_{>0}\(R_{>0} × A_f^×)/A^{×2} → Q^×\A^×/A^{×2} is therefore onto. It is also injective: x = q·y·a² with x_∞, y_∞ > 0 forces q > 0. So in the ramified case the image is the whole group, not an index-2 subgroup. Compactness: the parities of the p-adic valuations give a continuous surjection A^×/A^{×2} → ⊕_p Z/2, an infinite discrete group. In the split case Nrd maps G(A)/G(A)^+ onto A^×/A^{×2}, so that quotient is not compact either. Only the quotients by Q^× (by G(Q)) are compact. Proposition 3.6 uses only ker(χ_{E_0}∘Nrd), so nothing downstream changes.
findings.fix: In item 8 replace 'a monomorphism of compact abelian groups' by 'a monomorphism of locally compact abelian groups'. Replace 'so the second map is onto in the split case and has index-2 image otherwise' by 'and the second map is a bijection in both cases (when B is ramified at ∞ its image is Q_{>0}\(R_{>0} × A_f^×)/A^{×2}, which maps isomorphically onto Q^×\A^×/A^{×2} because −1 ∈ Q^×)'. Add source issues at §2.3, p. 162, and §3.3, proof of Proposition 3.6, p. 172 (arXiv v3 §2.3 and Proposition 18): index 2 (kind error, affects nothing downstream) and 'compact' (kind misprint).

findings.where: PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19 items (no item); route 1 brief; prerequisites
findings.claim: Duke's theorem, in the form the paper uses, has no item. That form is: the periodic measures on toral packets [T_i(A)g_i] ⊂ [G(A)], for an arbitrary Q-form G of PGL_2, with |D_i| → ∞ and a fixed split prime, converge to G(A)^+-invariant probability measures, including non-escape of mass. The paper proves it by Linnik's method [Lin68]. It is used three times in the main proof: tightness in Corollary 3.5, the marginals in Lemma 4.7 and Theorem 4.4, and 'µ is a probability measure' in Lemma 10.1. Item 1 and item 27 mention it only in their notes. The brief calls it an 'external input' listed as a prerequisite, but the prerequisite list has only Duke's modular-surface theorem [Duk88] and Iwaniec, not Linnik [Lin68]. PAPER-DUKE-IMAMOGLU-TOTH-16 route 1 (GN.3–GN.4, e.g. its item 53, genus-restricted equidistribution of CM points on the modular surface) plans only the split, non-adelic special case.
findings.evidence: Published p. 176 (before Theorem 4.4): 'The essential ingredient in the proof of the following theorem is the joinings theorem of Einsiedler and Lindenstrauss [EL15a, Th. 1.4] and Duke's theorem for equidistribution in the absolute rank 1 case. Notice that because we assume a fixed split prime, the equidistribution in the absolute rank 1 case that we use is already covered by Linnik's method [Lin68].' P. 171, proof of Corollary 3.5: 'Because this sequence of measures is tight by Duke's theorem'. P. 178, proof of Lemma 4.7: 'Because of Duke's theorem, proved by Linnik under the assumption of a fixed split prime, µ projects in each coordinate to a G(A)^+-invariant measure on [G(A)]'. P. 238, proof of Lemma 10.1: 'From Duke's theorem we know that µ is a probability measure.' The prerequisites array of the extraction has no entry for Linnik, Ergodic Properties of Algebraic Fields (1968).
findings.fix: Add an item 'Duke's theorem for toral packets on [G(A)] (Linnik's form)', stated with its hypotheses. G is a Q-form of PGL_2; T_i are maximal Q-anisotropic tori; the toral sets [T_i(A)g_i] satisfy (♠) at a fixed prime p_1 split in every E_i; and |D_i| → ∞. The conclusion is that the periodic measures are tight and every limit is G(A)^+-invariant. The locator is §4, p. 176, and its uses are Corollary 3.5, Lemma 4.7 and Lemma 10.1. Route it to route 1 (the Part II) as an imported statement. Its note should say that for B = M_2 it specialises the Duke-type equidistribution routed by PAPER-DUKE-IMAMOGLU-TOTH-16 to GN.4, and that the Part II must state the adelic form with the split-prime hypothesis. Add [Lin68] to the prerequisites.

findings.where: PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19 prerequisites (Huxley entry and omissions); route 1 brief; PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19/95, PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19/124
findings.claim: The prerequisite entry for Huxley says the bound 'is not needed for the main theorem'. It is needed: with van der Corput's θ_l > 2/3 and Gelbart–Jacquet's θ = 1/2, the two ranges of §10.4 do not overlap. The proof closes only with Huxley's exponent or with a bound towards Ramanujan better than 1/2 (Shahidi, Luo–Rudnick–Sarnak). The route 1 brief ends its 'assembly' with the cross-correlation bound (the large-norm range, item 123). It never plans the small-norm range (item 124), which rests on several inputs: the Ellenberg–Michel–Venkatesh argument with Linnik's basic lemma for one-sided Bowen balls; Hecke-operator norm bounds from a bound θ towards Ramanujan together with Jacquet–Langlands; Siegel's ineffective lower bound; and the maximal-entropy bootstrap. It does not name the lattice-point or Ramanujan input that closes the gap. The review flagged Conrey–Iwaniec, Hecke/Landau [Lan18], [Sar91], [BS91], [CU04], [COU01] and [JL70] as missing from the prerequisites (notes of items 99 and 124) but did not add them. Also absent: Siegel's theorem, [Lin68], Gelbart–Jacquet, [Sha88]/[LRS99], and [EL10]/[MT94] for the entropy step.
findings.evidence: Published p. 256: 'To conclude the proof we need to verify that the range of (55) overlaps with the range of (59). Taking θ_l > 2/3 from Van der Corput's bound [vdC20] and θ = 1/2 from Gelbart-Jacquet, we see that any improvement to either bound would imply the necessary overlap in ranges. This can be achieved either by taking a smaller admissible value of θ_l such as provided by [Hux03] or using any improvement towards Ramanujan beyond θ ≤ 1/2 as in [Sha88], [LRS99].' At θ_l = 2/3 and θ = 1/2 both thresholds (2 − θ_l^{−1})/3 and 1/(2 + 2/(1−θ)) equal 1/6; item 124 itself records this. P. 255: 'Linnik's Basic Lemma for one-sided Bowen balls in this setting (cf. [EMV13]) applies only for m ∈ N in the range (58) 𝔑_i p_1^m ≤ |D|^{1/2+o(1)}, where the o(1) is ineffective as it is derived from Siegel's bound.' The brief's final clause lists only 'the reduction of the main theorem to a bound on cross-correlation, the identification of the shifted convolution …, the ellipse …, and the final bound with its saving p_1^{−2n}'. It does not contain the words Linnik, Ramanujan, Huxley or Siegel's theorem.
findings.fix: Rewrite the Huxley prerequisite's 'why': the paper needs either Huxley's admissible exponent θ_l > 131/208 or a bound θ < 1/2 towards Ramanujan to make the two ranges of §10.4 overlap. Add prerequisites for Linnik [Lin68], Siegel (1935), Conrey–Iwaniec (2000), Landau [Lan18], Gelbart–Jacquet (1978), Shahidi [Sha88], Luo–Rudnick–Sarnak [LRS99], Clozel–Ullmo [CU04], Clozel–Oh–Ullmo [COU01], Sarnak [Sar91], Burger–Sarnak [BS91], Jacquet–Langlands [JL70], Margulis–Tomanov [MT94] and Einsiedler–Lindenstrauss [EL10]. Extend the route 1 brief's assembly with the small-norm range: the EMV argument, Linnik's basic lemma, the Hecke norm gap from θ and Jacquet–Langlands, and the entropy bootstrap. Also have the brief state the overlap lemma, naming Huxley's exponent (GN.4, route 5) or a bound θ < 1/2 imported from the atlas's automorphic roadmaps as the input that closes the gap.

findings.where: PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19 route 3 (HeegnerPointEulerSystems:HE.0), genus-theory block: items 101–107, 119, 120; notes of items 102, 104, 106, 119
findings.claim: The notes of items 102, 104, 106 and 119 treat the maximal-order case as only planned by the Tau Ceti Multiquadratic roadmap of the genus theory. That case is already built in the Tau Ceti library at the pinned commit f790474: the principal genus theorem, and the formula 2-rank = t − 1 for imaginary quadratic fields. The notes cite no declaration. The rest of the block, genus theory for an arbitrary quadratic order, extends a Tau Ceti roadmap in its own direction. PROTOCOL §15–16 send that to a Part II of the Tau Ceti roadmap ('Tau Ceti roadmaps are never re-planned: what extends one is a Part II'), not to a proposed roadmap's layer that does not import it. HE.0's dependencies (GlobalNumberFields, ClassFieldTheory, NumberFieldArithmetic, H4–H5) do not include Multiquadratic. The review's verdict on route 3 says only that 'Tau Ceti Multiquadratic layer 3 already plans the genus-field description of Cl/Cl²'. A Part II in exactly this direction was accepted later the same day (PAPER-DUKE-IMAMOGLU-TOTH-16 route 10, MultiquadraticPartII, whose design job DESIGN-MultiquadraticPartII is pending). findings.claim: The paper has further slips that the extraction and review did not record, and three recorded corrections are incomplete or partly wrong. (a) Lemma 10.1 assumes the cross-correlation bound 'for all ξ ∈ (G × G)(A)', while §10.4 proves it via Theorem 8.7, which needs ctr(ξ)_{p_1} ∈ A_{p_1}. This is a gap, harmless because the proof of Lemma 10.1 uses only ξ ∈ Ξ_1; item 123 repeats 'every ξ'. (b) The first display of the proof of Proposition 10.13 (p. 248) has 'ω log ω' where Lemma 10.11 gives |ω|², the same slip as E28. (c) In (56)–(57), p. 254–255, ‖T_{p_j^m}‖_0 ≪ … p_j^{−m(1−θ+ε)/2} has the ε-loss with the wrong sign; it should be 1 − θ − ε. This is harmless because (59) keeps a margin ε_1; item 124 copies it. (d) E7 should add that Λ_∞ in Definition 2.4(2) lacks the conjugation by g_∞ that Definition 2.1 and Remark 2.5 use. (e) E12's correction misses that the proof on p. 179 also writes 'L(Q_S) ∩ G(Q_S)^+' for (G × G)(Q_S)^+. (f) E13 offers 'or require π^{2k+1} = ε', which is not always possible.
findings.evidence: (a) P. 238, Lemma 10.1: 'for all ξ ∈ (G × G)(A)'. P. 253, §10.4: 'Let ξ ∈ (G × G)(A). … we can use Proposition 10.15 and Theorem 8.7'. Theorem 8.7 (p. 203) and Proposition 8.30 are stated 'with ctr(ξ)_{p_1} ∈ A_{p_1}'. The proof of Lemma 10.1 restricts to 'Ξ_1 := {ξ ∈ G^Δ(A)^+\(G × G)(A) | ctr(ξ)_{p_1} ∈ A_{p_1}, ctr(ξ)_{p_2} ∈ A_{p_2}}'. (b) arXiv v3 source, first display of the proof of Proposition 151, '\omega\log\omega'; the statement and Lemma 10.11 have |ω|². (c) Bounds towards Ramanujan give decay p^{−m(1−θ)/2} up to a factor polynomial in m, which is ≪_ε p^{−m(1−θ−ε)/2}, not the stronger p^{−m(1−θ+ε)/2}. (d) P. 166: 'Let Λ_∞ ⊂ E(R) be the intersection of the closed unit ball of ‖•‖_∞ with E(R)'. P. 165, Definition 2.1: 'Λ_v := E(Q_v) ∩ g_vO_vg_v^{−1}'. Remark 2.5 derives D_∞ = 1 from g_∞^{−1}T(R)g_∞ = K_∞, which has content only for the conjugated ball. (e) P. 179, proof of Lemma 4.8: 'on [L_Sg_S] for some g_S ∈ G(Q_S) and L_S of finite index in L(Q_S) ∩ G(Q_S)^+'. (f) Write ε = π^{2k+1}u. Replacing π by πw changes u by w^{−(2k+1)}, so π^{2k+1} = ε is possible only when u is a (2k+1)-th power. For v = 7, k = 1, ε = 7³·3 it is impossible, since 3 is not a cube mod 7 (the cubes of units mod 7 are ±1).
findings.fix: Add source issues (a) (gap, affects the proof), (b) (misprint, or fold it into E28) and (c) (misprint). Extend E7 with (d) and E12 with (e). Delete the alternative 'or require π^{2k+1} = ε' from E13's correction, keeping the reading ((α, επ^{−k}β), (π^{−k}·^σβ, ^σα)). In item 123 restrict ξ to ctr(ξ)_{p_1} ∈ A_{p_1}, and in item 124 write 1 − θ − ε.
